answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: honest seeds retain probability mass according to transition probabilities, while an adversarial Sybil cluster—an ember, opal, and juniper-labeled region—is separated by a sparse external cut. Its low conductance limits escape and entry flow; min-cut transitivity bounds the cluster’s stationary mass, and thus aggregate voting weight, by boundary-to-volume ratio rather than population.
